caption:
Quinn's new e-scooter met a tram track on a wet morning, and Quinn landed on a hand. The wrist still moved, so it must be fine… right?

Kay's take: being able to move your wrist doesn't rule out a fracture. Speed and small wheels mean wrists and heads often take the hit.

What can help: a helmet on every ride, speed that suits the surface, extra care on wet roads, gutters and tram tracks, taking it easy on the first rides of a new vehicle, and a graded return after injury with strength, balance and grip work.

Get it checked after a head knock with headache, dizziness or poor focus, bony tenderness or swelling lasting more than a couple of days, or a dislocation.
